correctness.rationale: For a prescribed lifted arc \(xy\) over a base arc \(u\to v\), Alspach supplies a base \(t\)-cycle through \(u\to v\) for every \(3\le t\le c\). Every target length \(\ell\in[3,c\alpha]\) belongs to some integer interval \([3k,ck]\) with \(1\le k\le\alpha\) because \(c\ge5\) makes consecutive intervals overlap or touch. Writing \(\ell\) as a sum of \(k\) admissible base lengths and lifting the \(j\)-th base cycle into the \(j\)-th clone layer yields a simple directed cycle: each segment is directed, the last vertex of each base cycle points to \(u\) and therefore to the next \(u\)-clone, distinct layers prevent repeated vertices, and the first lifted base arc is the prescribed \(xy\). The verifier independently reconstructs and checks this construction on several regular base tournaments. The \(c=3\) boundary is explicitly excluded and fails for \(\alpha\ge2\).

evidence: Xia 2026: every regular \(c\)-partite tournament is \(4\)-arc-pancyclic for \(c\ge93\); for \(c\ge7\) it guarantees a long initial interval of cycle lengths, not the full spectrum from \(3\) through \(c\alpha\) in general.
Pan--Zhang 2004: each arc lies on a cycle meeting exactly \(k\) partite sets for \(k=4,\ldots,c\); cycle vertex length is not fixed when partite sets have size greater than one.

originality.rationale: The 2026 initiating paper proves \(4\)-arc-pancyclicity only for all regular multipartite tournaments with at least \(93\) parts and gives weaker distinct-length guarantees for smaller part counts; it does not state the equal-blow-up preservation theorem. Alspach covers only the unblown regular tournament. Pan--Zhang controls the number of partite sets met by cycles, not every vertex length. Yeo-type vertex-pancyclicity does not imply arc-pancyclicity. Targeted web and semantic-research-index searches for blow-up/composition/lexicographic-product formulations returned no covering theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a broad, natural infinite subclass of regular multipartite tournaments for which the strongest possible prescribed-arc cycle spectrum holds, strengthening the recent general 4-arc-pancyclic direction without a large-number-of-parts assumption. It also isolates a reusable additive splicing mechanism for digraph compositions: multiple base cycles through one arc can be concatenated across independent clone layers to realize all intermediate lengths. This directly informs the current conjectural landscape for arc-pancyclicity in regular multipartite tournaments and is not merely a parameter recomputation or isolated small case.
